title: Invertible sheaves on a finite pinching square
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $v:X'\to X$ and $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be $S$-morphisms, with $v$ finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and $j$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $Z'=X'\times_XZ$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $j':Z'\to X'$ and $w:Z'\to Z$. Assume that $X$ has an affine open cover by $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] such that $v^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z\times_XU=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $Z'\times_XU=\operatorname{Spec}F$, the map $A\to F$ is surjective, and the canonical map $R\to A\times_FB$ is an isomorphism. Here $A\times_FB=\{(a,b):a|_F=b|_F\}$, with coordinatewise ring operations. Pullback gives an equivalence between invertible sheaves on $X$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and triples $(M,N,\alpha)$, where $M$ is invertible on $X'$, $N$ is invertible on $Z$, and $\alpha:(j')^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}w^*N$ is an isomorphism on $Z'$. A morphism of triples is a pair of module maps commuting with $\alpha$; thus the equivalence also identifies automorphisms. The equivalence respects tensor products. It is natural for every base change $T\to S$ for which the base-changed square again has this affine fibre-product description. In particular it is natural for flat base changes. Empty $Z$ is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0D2J (lemma-finitely-presented-module-over-fibre-product), with Tag 07RU (lemma-module-over-fibre-product), applied to rank-one finite projectives and glued on the stated affine cover. Tensor and base-change naturality are the canonical pullback comparisons.

proof.text: Fix a chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ in the assumed cover. Write $M_A=\Gamma(v^{-1}U,M)$ and $N_B=\Gamma(Z\times_XU,N)$. The affine invertible-sheaf dictionary makes these finite projectives of rank one, and the affine pullback formula turns $\alpha$ into $F\otimes_A M_A\simeq F\otimes_B N_B$. Apply finite-projective patching to construct the actual module $P_U=\{(m,n):\alpha(1\otimes m)=1\otimes n\}$. It is finite projective over $R$, and its two scalar extensions, with their specified comparison on $F$, are precisely the given modules and comparison. On morphisms the construction sends $(a,b)$ to the restriction of $a\oplus b$ to this kernel. The affine tilde equivalence turns module homomorphisms into all morphisms of the associated quasi-coherent sheaves. The general patched-module comparison gives these projection counits even before imposing finite projectivity.

The finite projective $P_U$ has rank one at every prime. Indeed put $J=\ker(R\to B)$; surjectivity of $A\to F$ shows $R\to B$ is surjective and identifies $J$ with $\ker(A\to F)$. If $\mathfrak p\supseteq J$, let $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p/J\in\operatorname{Spec}B$. A standard-open free neighbourhood of $\mathfrak p$ for $P_U$ has some rank $d$. After tensoring its fibre with $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, the projection comparison identifies it with the rank-one fibre of $N_B$, so $d=1$. If $\mathfrak p\not\supseteq J$, choose $r\in J\setminus\mathfrak p$. Localizing $0\to R\to A\oplus B\to F\to0$ at $r$ gives $R_r=A_r$, since $B_r=F_r=0$. Hence $\mathfrak p$ corresponds to a prime of $A_r$; the same free-neighbourhood and fibre calculation, now with $M_A$, gives rank one. Principal-open sections of $\widetilde {P_U}$ are these localizations, so these rank-one free neighbourhoods trivialize $L_U=\widetilde {P_U}$. Thus $L_U$ is invertible. Conversely an invertible sheaf on $U$ has finite projective rank-one sections by the affine dictionary, and the unit of patching recovers those sections. Consequently pullback on this chart is fully faithful on all module maps and essentially surjective on line-bundle triples.

source.place: Tags 0D2J and 07RU; Algebra Tag 00NX; Schemes Tag 01HV

proof.text: These constructions commute with principal-open restriction. For $r\in R$, exactness of localization applied to the two kernels $R=\ker(A\oplus B\to F)$ and $P_U=\ker(M_A\oplus N_B\to F\otimes_BN_B)$ identifies $R_r=A_r\times_{F_r}B_r$ and $(P_U)_r=\{(m,n)\in(M_A)_r\oplus(N_B)_r:\alpha_r(1\otimes m)=1\otimes n\}$. The ring map $A_r\to F_r$ remains surjective: a preimage of a fraction is obtained by lifting its numerator. The principal-open descriptions of tilde sections identify the localized projection maps with the restricted projection maps. Therefore the fully faithful affine equivalence of steps 1--2 also holds on every such principal open.

source.place: Tag 00CS (Algebra, proposition-localization-exact); the argument of more-algebra lemma-diagram-localize

proof.text: For charts $U_i,U_j$, their intersection has a cover by opens principal in both affine charts. On each such open, step 3 and affine full faithfulness give a unique isomorphism $L_{U_i}\simeq L_{U_j}$ inducing the identity on the prescribed triple. On smaller opens the maps agree, because they agree on a principal-open basis and affine full faithfulness is faithful there. Glue these maps over the intersection. On triple intersections their two possible composites induce the same identity triple, and equality can again be checked on a principal-open basis inside one chart. Thus the transition maps satisfy the cocycle condition. Gluing modules produces $L$ on $X$, invertible because this is local on $X$, with the desired pullback identifications. The same argument glues the unique local lift of any morphism of triples. It also proves uniqueness of that lift globally. Thus pullback is an equivalence of the categories stated in the item. Applying the bijection on Hom sets to invertible endomorphisms identifies automorphisms as well: lifts of an inverse are inverse by faithfulness.

source.place: Sheaves Tags 04TN, 00AL and 00AM; Schemes principal-open basis and common principal refinements

proof.text: For two triples take their tensor product componentwise and tensor their overlap identifications. The sheaf $L_1\otimes L_2$ is invertible, and the canonical pullback comparisons identify its triple with that tensor-product triple: on simple tensors the comparison is $(1\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)\mapsto1\otimes(x\otimes y)$. Full faithfulness yields the unique comparison between $L_1\otimes L_2$ and the sheaf reconstructed from the tensor-product triple. Its inverse lifts the inverse triple map. The unit comparison uses the diagonal identification $R=A\times_FB$ on each chart. The associativity, symmetry and unit diagrams commute because their pullbacks act identically on the displayed simple tensors, and pullback is faithful. This proves tensor compatibility.

source.place: Modules Tag 01CT (lemma-constructions-invertible); canonical tensor and composition comparisons

proof.text: Let $T\to S$ be a base change satisfying the stated affine hypothesis. Pullback of the reconstructed $L$ to $X_T$ is invertible. Its restrictions to $X^{\prime}_T$ and $Z_T$ identify with the pulled-back $M,N$ by the canonical composition comparison for pullback; on $Z^{\prime}_T$ the overlap comparison is the pullback of $\alpha$. Apply the equivalence already proved on the new square: full faithfulness gives a unique isomorphism from the reconstruction of this new triple to $L|_{X_T}$ inducing those identifications. This is natural in triple morphisms by faithfulness. For two successive allowed base changes the composite comparison and the direct comparison induce the same maps on both components, by the pullback composition formula, so are equal. The identity base change likewise gives the identity. This establishes the asserted naturality without claiming that tensoring an arbitrary kernel is exact.

source.place: Modules Tag 01CT; composition comparisons and uniqueness under the equivalence

proof.text: Finally suppose $T\to S$ is flat. The map $X_T\to X$ is flat by flat base change; on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq X_T$ mapping into a chosen $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, the affine criterion makes $C$ flat over $R$. The three inverse-image charts have rings $A\otimes_R C$, $B\otimes_R C$, $F\otimes_R C$ by the affine fibre-product formula. Tensoring $0\to R\to A\oplus B\to F\to0$ with $C$ preserves its kernel, so $C\cong(A\otimes_R C)\times_{F\otimes_R C}(B\otimes_R C)$. Surjectivity of the first map to $F\otimes_R C$ follows by lifting numerators of simple tensors. Finite generation of $A$ over $R$ persists by tensoring a finite list of generators, and $R\to B$ being a quotient remains a quotient after tensoring. Thus the base-changed square satisfies all the hypotheses on an affine cover, and step 6 applies. If $Z$ is empty, then $B=F=0$ on every chart, $R=A$ and $P_U=M_A$. There is a unique module on the empty scheme and a unique overlap identification, so the same construction gives precisely the asserted equivalence, including automorphisms and tensor products.

It gives the full-subcategory equivalence on all module maps, the quasi-inverse K = M x_{F(x)M} N, the counits from 07RU and the unit from 0D2I(2). It is statement-only and self-contained, and a DAG search found no duplicate. lem-sfb-patched-module-base-change is only its counit sub-clause, and the other 08KH-family nodes cover flat algebras, topology or scheme pushouts. Mathlib has only RingHom.pullback. The item statement is unchanged and holds for empty Z, Z=X and the identity square. Step by step: step 1 uses the affine dictionary, the pullback-section formula on j' and w, and the tilde adjunction. Step 2 shows rank one by the conductor J: p containing J via B, kappa(p)=kappa(q); p not containing J via R_r = A_r. Step 3 (elementary) localizes the kernels. Step 4 glues on opens principal in both charts (01HR), so intersections of affines are never assumed affine, and applies glue (1)/(2). Step 5 checks tensor coherence by faithfulness. Step 6 covers allowed base changes by uniqueness. Step 7 handles flat base change: X_T->X is flat, R->C is flat, the charts are A(x)C etc., and flat-tensor-exact keeps the fibre product. That covers the parent's arbitrary T over a field. Every cited unit is on the route, the declared tool_uses are generic, and no SGA is cited.
